stories.title: Man sentenced to life for assaulting minor sister-in-law
summary: PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has set aside the acquittal of a medical doctor and sentenced him to life imprisonment with fine of Rs500,000 for sexually assaulting his 12-year-old sister-in-law over three years ago.
A bench consisting of Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah Khan accepted an appeal filed by the victim and declared that the trial court had erred in acquitting the suspect.
PHC accepts appeal of victim, sets aside acquittal order of trial court An additional sessions judge/child protection court had acquitted the suspect on Nov 11, 2025 in the case.

stories.title: Police set up eight pickets for PAF base security in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Eight special police pickets have been set up at various locations to ensure the security of the PAF base.

As part of the security plan for the eight pickets, police mobile squads from Chaklala, Sadiqabad and Waris Khan police stations will patrol around Nur Khan PAF Base, while the Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force have been assigned patrol duties around the base.
At the TM Chowk police picket, the RA Bazaar police, Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force will patrol within the limits of the R.A.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority appoints three new directors general
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has completed the recruitment process for three new directors general (DGs) in BS-20.
According to CDA officials, retired Brig Mohammad Javed Iqbal, retired Brig Rashid Manzoor and retired Brig Azhar Khan have been appointed as DGs.
However, after the stay was vacated, the CDA completed the recruitment process and issued notifications appointing the new DGs.

stories.title: Jhelum's ancient Padhri village faces relentless erosion
summary: Located at the foot of Tilla Jogian, Padhri village is another place dotted with astonishing examples of stone architecture typical of the Salt Range terrain.

Syed Ahmed, another resident, while guiding this correspondent through the streets, said all the houses had been built with grey stones brought from the surrounding hills of Tarakki, Domeli and Tilla Jogian.
A centuries-old small mosque, featuring a highly attractive facade built with sandy grey stones, is another marvel of stone craftsmanship in the Domeli and Tilla region.

stories.title: 120 Swabi schools sealed over poor building conditions
summary: SWABI: The district administration has sealed around 120 schools, mostly private, in different parts of Swabi after inspections revealed that their buildings were unsafe for students, sources said on Sunday.

The sources told Dawn that inspections conducted in all four tehsils of the district found cracks in the walls and rooms of several school buildings, making them unfit for educational activities and posing a threat to students’ lives.
The deputy commissioner said the district had a total of 289,180 students, adding that the administration did not have separate figures for children enrolled in private schools.

stories.title: CM inaugurates Rs250m Sindhi Muslim Food Walk
summary: According to an official statement, the urban improvement project aims to promote food and cultural tourism, facilitating local businesses, improving civic infrastructure and providing residents and visitors with a better environment to enjoy the city’s rich culinary culture.
The chief minister said Sindhi Muslim was already among Karachi’s well-known commercial and food destinations, attracting visitors from different parts of the city.

He said the Food Walk was not merely a beautification scheme but a comprehensive urban improvement initiative designed to make the area more accessible, attractive, organised and convenient for businesses, visitors and residents.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Development Authority plans major road rehabilitation scheme
summary: RAWALPINDI: After sitting idle for one year, the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has planned road rehabilitation and infrastructure improvement works in the garrison city at an estimated cost of Rs68.98 million.

A senior official of RDA told Dawn that in the last one year the civic agency was looking after Rawalpindi Ring Road project worth Rs47 billion, while no development work was launched for rehabilitation of roads.

He said that the new proposed development scheme, “Framework Agreement for Rehabilitation/Repair of Roads, Footpaths, Storm Water Drains, Manholes and Road Marking at Different Roads of City”, aims to address the repair and maintenance of urban road infrastructure.

Dr Aneel Kumar, who liaisons between the DC Office and the health department, said that thanks to transportation provided to the workers, they are also able to keep the vaccine fresh the entire day. “Their ice packs used to melt.

stories.title: Tapping the potential of 5G
summary: Though networks cover over 92pc of Pakistan, the GSMA estimates only 58pc of adults used mobile internet in 2025, held back by affordability, digital literacy and social norms.
The digital value Pakistan creates should be captured, and compounded, at home: freelancers exporting services, start-ups scaling on local cloud, talent competing globally without emigrating.
The real question is not how much faster 5G can make a phone, but how far it can take Pakistan.

stories.title: Man kills wife, injures five children with knife in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A man allegedly killed his wife and injured their five children, attacking them with a knife, in the jurisdiction of Nishtar Colony police here on Sunday.
Annoyed by her refusal, the suspect attacked his wife with a knife and also injured the children when they tried to rescue their mother.
ENCOUNTER: A suspect was allegedly killed during an alleged encounter with the police in Shahdara Town here on Sunday.

stories.title: Mobile phone shop owner hospitalised after ‘police torture’ in Kasur
summary: KASUR: A mobile shop owner was hospitalised after being critically injured in alleged police torture at his shop in the Mobile Market, Railway Road, Kot Radha Kishan, the other day.
Footage of the incident went viral on social media.

However, on Sunday, Kot Radha Kishan police booked 40 suspects, 15 of them nominated, on charges of attacking police, tearing off their uniform, snatching cash and getting the suspect (shopkeeper) released from custody.

stories.title: Factory worker dies, eight injured in gas cylinder blast in Lahore's Gulberg
summary: LAHORE: A worker died while his eight colleagues were injured, three of them critically, when a gas cylinder exploded in a factory on the Gurumangat Road, Gulberg, on Sunday.
The blast took place on the first floor of the Shezan Bakers factory where more than 40 employees were busy at work.
A spokesperson for Rescue 1122 said that as a result of the blast , a part of the building collapsed which occurred soon after leakage in the gas cylinder.

stories.title: Reko Diq project may face further delay
summary: Production at the Reko Diq copper-gold project could be delayed by two years to 2030, pending improved security in Balochistan and de-escalation in the Middle East crisis, according to government sources and industry insiders.
Canadian mining titan Barrick Mining (formerly Gold) Corporation is expected to resume full-scale development by mid-2027 following an ongoing internal project review.
In February this year, Barrick Mining initiated a formal review of Reko Diq, announcing a slowdown in development and extending its assessment period through early 2027.

stories.title: BRICS accelerates green transition

In 2025, the BRICS leaders endorsed a broad climate leadership agenda and adopted a cooperation framework for climate finance.

Following the BRICS leaders’ call on multilateral development banks to enhance collaboration with climate funds, the NDB could explore partnership agreements with the Green Climate Fund and the Adaptation Fund.

stories.title: Gilgit-Baltistan celebrates 79 years of independence
summary: GILGIT: The 79th Independence Day of Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) was celebrated across the region on Sunday with traditional zeal and fervour, marked by military parades, cultural festivities, polo competitions and tributes to the heroes who liberated the homeland from Dogra rule.
On Nov 1, 1947, the GB Scouts liberated the region from the Dogra Raj and raised the flag of freedom, declaring an independent state that later joined Pakistan.

A morning flag-hoisting ceremony was held at the historic Chinar Bagh in Gilgit, attended by Governor Syed Mehdi Shah, Chief Minister Amjad Hussain, Force Commander GB Maj Gen Tajdeed Mumtaz, ministers, elected representatives, and civil and military officials.

War is Interested in You: The Breakdown of International Order and the Threat of World War Three by distinguished British columnist Gideon Rachman is an insightful book on a subject that is especially relevant today.
While acts of war are the most dramatic examples of the breakdown of the rules-based order, Rachman argues that international institutions are crumbling in other ways too.

stories.title: Karachi Port Trust handles ships with 101,000 tonnes of cargo
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Karachi Port Trust (KPT) has simultaneously handled two foreign bulk carriers carrying a combined 101,000 tonnes of diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertiliser and wheat.

Announcing the development on Sunday, Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry said the concurrent unloading of the vessels underscored the port’s enhanced capacity to manage critical agricultural inputs and essential commodities efficiently.

KPT Chairman retired Rear Admiral Shahid Ahmed said Karachi Port played a vital role in the country’s trade and supply chain network, particularly in facilitating imports of agricultural inputs and essential food commodities.

After killing the two people and abducting Haider, the armed men fled to an undisclosed location.

stories.title: US-backed consortium proposes $4.4bn LNG project
summary: The first phase will comprise an LNG terminal and storage facility with four tanks and an estimated annual throughput of 35 billion cubic feet (BCF), at a cost of $1.7bn.
The SPV will develop, own and operate the project as a regional LNG storage, regasification and trading hub, serving Pakistan’s domestic gas market alongside US and Middle Eastern LNG suppliers.
The LNG terminal and storage facility will have four tanks, each with a capacity of 140,000 cubic metres, providing total static storage capacity of 560,000 cubic metres.

stories.title: Agriculture: How flawed wheat policy fuelled flour crisis
summary: The roots of the crisis lie in Punjab’s decision earlier this year to abandon conventional wheat procurement under pressure from lenders and replace it with a bureaucratically conceived scheme to engage private-sector aggregators to procure wheat on its behalf.
Disputes over financing terms deterred banks, while the substantial gap between the government’s procurement rate and the open-market price stalled farmers from selling to the aggregators.
Wheat would continue pouring in from private stocks but at a price of choice of those who control the supply.

The expansion of retail participation will ultimately be judged not by account numbers alone, but by whether small investors can invest with confidence, companies can attract capital on fair terms and the market maintains trust through both rising and falling cycles.

The minister said the expansion of the M4 Motorway would help ease traffic congestion, make travelling safer and more convenient and prevent road accidents.

He also instructed the authorities to ensure complete lighting arrangements along the Pindi-Bhattian-Faisalabad section of the Motorway and finalise designs of rest areas within one week to facilitate travellers.

stories.title: Pakistan outperforms Vietnam in rice exports
summary: Total worldwide trade of Basmati rice held firm at 6.9 million tonnes – matching 2025 levels – as buyers in key markets prioritised securing Pakistan and India’s signature premium grain over non-aromatic varieties.

The price premium highlights strong international demand for Pakistan’s mixed export basket of high-value aromatic Basmati and non-basmati varieties, competing directly with Southeast Asian competitors like Thailand and Vietnam, which export ‘Hom Mali’ and non-basmati rice.

Basmati exports absorb shock waves of the US-Iran conflict, sea route disruptions Hamid Malik, a rice industry expert, notes that market dynamics have been shifting since December 2025, when Pakistan surpassed Vietnam’s monthly export volume for the first time this millennium.

stories.title: Anti-polio drive begins today to vaccinate over 990,000 children in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: More than 990,000 children less than five years of age will get polio vaccination in the Rawalpindi district as a four-day campaign starts on Monday (today).

According to Punjab EOC Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz, the November campaign will continue for seven days in Lahore, while the remaining 12 districts will observe a four-day drive. “Every campaign is an important opportunity to protect children against polio.
Parents must ensure that all children under five receive polio drops during every campaign, even if they have been vaccinated in previous rounds,” said Mr Parvaiz.

stories.title: Student injured, police van damaged in Bannu blast
summary: BANNU: A motorcycle bomb exploded near a police mobile van within the jurisdiction of the cantonment police station, close to the Government Postgraduate College in Bannu, partially damaging the vehicle and reportedly injuring a student.
All police personnel remained unharmed, while a student was reportedly injured in the explosion.
Meanwhile, three policemen were injured when a quadcopter reportedly dropped explosives on Tower No. 3 of the temporary displaced persons’ camp in the Bakakhel area on Sunday, police sources said.

stories.title: Fading wheat cultivation ritual leaves Chitral residents deeply nostalgic
summary: CHITRAL: Chitral residents have expressed deep nostalgia over the gradual fading of ‘bi-nisik’, a centuries-old socio-agricultural custom that once filled the region with vibrant autumn festivities.
As per the book, the tradition of bi-nisik was practised in the Yasin Valley of Gilgit-Baltistan as well, apart from Chitral.

Prof Israruddin emphasised how deeply embedded the practice was in the local psyche, noting that an entire month in the traditional Khowar (Chitrali) calendar was named ‘Bi-nisik’ to honour the sowing season.
